findings.description: The conductor now launches whenever `pup status` says a launch would be allowed. But `pup status` prints `Launch: allowed` while the memory floor or the plan's usage hold would still refuse the launch. The kickoff also says `pup status` shows each limit, including the 1.5 GB floor, which it never prints.
findings.body:
The new conductor protocol makes the verdict from `pup status` the trigger for a launch:

```ts
'1. `pup status`, then `pup plan`. Whenever `pup status` says a launch would be ' +
'allowed, launch one planned task, then read `pup status` again before the next. Pick ' +
```

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/b93d3232bfa70686caa2fef88bc69c9c4c2d176a/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L1810-L1812

That verdict is built by `launchRoomLines`, which looks only at the backlog and the load. When neither is over its limit it prints `allowed`:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/b93d3232bfa70686caa2fef88bc69c9c4c2d176a/src/core/session-cap.service.ts#L224-L240

`printLaunchRoom` (`src/cli/index.ts` L1033-1043) prints these lines unchanged. `pup launch` refuses on two more checks: `assertMemoryFloor()` (under 1.5 GB available) in `assertRoomToLaunch`, and the usage hold (5-hour usage at 85% or 7-day at 90%). The CLI treats both as no-room refusals (`NO_ROOM_ERRORS`).

**Trigger:** a usage hold is active, which can last hours, or available memory drops under 1.5 GB, while the backlog and the load are both under their limits. `pup status` prints `Launch: allowed`. The conductor follows step 1 and runs `pup launch`, which is refused. It reads `pup status` again, sees `allowed` again, and repeats this for as long as the hold lasts. The kickoff has no instruction for a launch refusal. The old protocol did not check memory or usage either, but it never had a status line saying `allowed` while launch refuses.

The kickoff's Commands bullet also now ends with "(`pup status` shows each)" right after naming the 1.5 GB memory floor:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/b93d3232bfa70686caa2fef88bc69c9c4c2d176a/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L1782-L1786

No status path prints available memory. The usage line shows percentages but never says launches are on hold. Before this PR the text said "(`pup status` shows it)" about the usage limit alone, which was accurate.

**Fix (either works):** fold the memory floor and the usage hold into the `launchRoomLines` verdict, e.g. `refused (under 1.5 GB of memory available)`. Or change step 1 to launch only when status allows it and no usage hold is shown, say what to do on a refusal, and drop "shows each" for memory.

findings.description: The load check `load.average > load.cores` is written three times: in assertLaunchRoom, launchRoomLines, and the fix-round check in session-lifecycle.service.ts:548. The backlog check `minutes > budgetMinutes` is written twice. A threshold change has to edit every copy, or the `pup status` verdict drifts from what launch enforces. Use one isLoaded/isOverBudget helper each.

unlandedLine keeps four counters (printable, unnamed, more, rest) and joins with ' and ' twice, so it can print "a, b and 3 more and 1 unnamed". Print the first printable ids plus a single "(+N more)" count of everything else, and keep the PRINTABLE_ID filter.

`Number.isFinite(median)` can never be false: longestStage keeps only finite non-negative times, and percentile returns one of them. Drop the dead check so readers don't hunt for a NaN path that doesn't exist.

LockBacklogOverBudgetError and MachineLoadedError are Error subclasses declared inline in a service file. general.md §Code layout puts Error subclasses in the area's errors file, like session-lifecycle.errors.ts.
The exported interface LockBacklog is declared in a *.service.ts file. general.md §Type separation puts exported types in a *.types.ts file.

The gate-time bounds and windows (UNTIMED_GATE_MS, GATE_FLOOR_MS, GATE_CEILING_MS, LAND_WINDOW_MS, GATE_SAMPLE, STAGES_READ, …) live in the service file. general.md §No hardcoded values puts them in the area's *.constants.ts.

This comment says the file is read "as `maxSessions` reads its file", but this PR deleted `maxSessions`, so the comparison now points at nothing. Name readPlainFile's options instead, or drop the clause.
This JSDoc places the conductor's pid file "beside its session cap (decision 188)", but this PR stopped writing conductor/max-sessions. A reader looking for the cap file in the store finds nothing.

ADRs 0194, 0183, 0156 and 0168 still describe conductor/max-sessions and maxSessions in the present tense and get no "Amended by 0197" back-link. A reader of those ADRs is told about a cap file that no longer exists.
